plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall, sun-chasing stalks carry dinner-plate flower heads. Each head has a ring of golden petals around a dark, tightly packed center. Fields of them turn whole hillsides into a bright yellow sea in late summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer, typically August through September in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America, including the American Southwest such as Santa Fe, New Mexico, where it is native, and gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower. It is hundreds of tiny florets packed in a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence. Young buds also track the sun across the sky each day.

plants.name: Dimorphotheca sinuata
plants.description: In the arid Northern Cape, winter rains set off a spring flower show. Orange daisies with glossy petals and dark centers carpet the veld, among thousands of other wildflower species. They turn their faces toward the sun, then close up on cloudy days and in the evening.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere spring, from early August to the end of September
plants.funFact: Namaqualand's flower display is one of the world's great natural spectacles. The region has more than 3,500 plant species, and many of the seeds lie dormant in the soil for years until the right rains arrive.
